mainTopic: Those who refused to teach their skills, the meaning of 'the name of the wicked shall rot', and teachings about צדיקים and רשעים
overview: The amud opens with the end of a teaching: no one can take what Heaven set aside for another person. A ברייתא then describes the singing skill of הוגרס בן לוי, and another tells of בן קמצר, who refused to teach his skill of writing four letters at once and had no good excuse. So the verse "ושם רשעים ירקב" is applied to him and his companions. רבי אלעזר explains that the names of the wicked 'rot' because no one names children after them. רבינא objects from a boy named דואג, and the גמרא answers that the boy's terrible end proves the point. A series of teachings follows, many from רבי אלעזר and from רבי יוחנן, about צדיקים and רשעים: Torah sources for 'זכר צדיק לברכה' and 'שם רשעים ירקב', עובדיה and עשו, the world existing even for one צדיק, and ה׳ guarding the pious from sin. The amud ends with ריש לקיש's teaching that Heaven helps one who comes to purify himself, and a parable from דבי רבי ישמעאל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No one can take what is set aside for another
steps.stepSummary: The closing lines of a teaching: what is yours will be given to you, nobody can touch what is prepared for someone else, and one kingdom cannot overlap another even by a hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from your own they will give you. No person can touch what is prepared for someone else. And one kingdom cannot overlap with another kingdom, not even by the width of a hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started on the previous amud. Its point is that whatever is meant for you will reach you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that nobody loses by being replaced. What Heaven set aside for one person cannot be taken by another. The kingdom example shows this exactly: when one kingdom's time ends, the next begins, with not a moment stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: What is prepared (set aside) for another person
Even the width of a hair

steps.whatToRemember: Whatever Heaven has set aside for a person, no one else can take, not even a hairbreadth.

phrases.english: And from your own they will give you.
phrases.notes: The last part of a three-part saying that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: No person can touch what is prepared for his fellow.
And one kingdom does not touch (overlap) another
even by the width of a hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a teaching begun earlier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every person and every kingdom receives exactly its own allotted share; no one can take another's.

steps.title: How הוגרס בן לוי sang
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes הוגרס בן לוי's singing technique, which was so powerful that the כהנים were thrown backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned הוגרס בן לוי. A ברייתא taught: when he sang a sweet melody, he put his thumb into his mouth and placed his finger between the strings, until his fellow כהנים were suddenly jolted backward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's mention of הוגרס בן לוי. It quotes a ברייתא that describes what his secret singing skill was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that he refused to teach his skill. The ברייתא now tells us what that skill was. He made a special sound with his thumb in his mouth and his finger on the strings, and it was so moving that the כהנים were thrown backward.

phrases.english: Hugras ben Levi, etc.
It was taught: when he would give his voice in a sweet melody,
he would put his thumb into his mouth,
and place his finger between the strings,
until his brothers the priests
were suddenly thrown backward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next person mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הוגרס בן לוי's secret skill was a special singing technique that overwhelmed his listeners.

steps.title: בן קמצר's special writing skill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בן קמצר refused to teach his skill. He could hold four pens and write a four-letter word all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בן קמצר did not want to teach the skill of writing. They said about him that he would take four pens between his fingers, and if there was a word of four letters, he would write it all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about another person who kept a skill secret, בן קמצר. It explains what his special skill was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the people in the משנה, בן קמצר refused to share his talent. His skill was writing all four letters of a four-letter word at the same time, with one pen between each pair of fingers. This sets up the question of why he refused to teach it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Ben Kamtzar

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַכְּתָב.
phrases.english: did not want to teach the craft of writing.
They said about him that he would take
four quills between his fingers,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיְתָה תֵּיבָה שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת
phrases.english: and if there was a word of four letters
he would write it all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּן קַמְצָר לֹא רָצָה לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of someone who would not teach his skill.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן קמצר had a unique writing skill and refused to teach it.

steps.title: בן קמצר is asked why he would not teach
steps.stepSummary: The people asked בן קמצר why he refused to teach. The others had a good answer, but he had none.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What reason did you see not to teach? All the others found an answer for their behavior, but בן קמצר did not find an answer for his.
steps.whatsHappening: בן קמצר is asked to explain why he refused to teach. Unlike the others, he could not give a good reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other people who kept their skills secret had a worthy reason. They worried their skill would be misused, for example for idol worship. בן קמצר had no such reason, which shows he kept his skill to himself only for his own honor.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see (what was your reason)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that everyone who refused to teach was criticized in the same way. The first group (בית גרמו and בית אבטינס) had a good answer and are called righteous. בן קמצר and his companions had no excuse.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה רָאִיתָ שֶׁלֹּא לְלַמֵּד?
phrases.english: They said to him: What did you see that you did not teach?
All of them found an answer for their conduct,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן קַמְצָר לֹא מָצָא תְּשׁוּבָה לִדְבָרָיו.
phrases.english: Ben Kamtzar did not find an answer for his conduct.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה רָאִיתָ שֶׁלֹּא לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the refusal described in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did בן קמצר refuse to teach his skill?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He had no good answer, unlike the others.

steps.title: The verses about the righteous and the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The first group is praised with "the memory of the righteous is a blessing." בן קמצר and those like him get "the name of the wicked shall rot."
steps.simpleTranslation: About the first group it says: "The memory of the righteous shall be a blessing." About בן קמצר and his companions it says: "But the name of the wicked shall rot."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by using one verse from משלי to judge both groups. The ones with good reasons are praised, and those without good reasons are criticized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group mentioned earlier (people like the house of גרמו and the house of אבטינס, who had a good excuse) are remembered for blessing. בן קמצר and his companions, who had no good excuse, are matched with the second half of the verse. That second half is what the גמרא will now explain.

keyTerms.meaning: The memory of the righteous is for a blessing (משלי י:ז)
And the name of the wicked shall rot

steps.whatToRemember: Holding back a skill for a good reason earns praise, but holding it back only for personal honor earns the label "the name of the wicked shall rot."

phrases.english: About the first ones it is said:
"The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing,"
and about Ben Kamtzar and his companions it is said:
"But the name of the wicked shall rot."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final judgment based on who had a good answer and who did not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Those with good reasons are remembered for blessing; בן קמצר and his companions are remembered as wicked whose name rots.

steps.title: What does "the name of the wicked shall rot" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a name can "rot."
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "But the name of the wicked shall rot" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The verse was just quoted, so the גמרא asks what it means. This sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A name is not a physical object, so it cannot literally rot. The גמרא wants to know what actually happens to a wicked person's name.

phrases.english: What is "But the name of the wicked shall rot"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the verse quoted at the end of step 5.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: people stop using their names
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that decay spreads over the names of the wicked, because people do not name their children after them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Rot comes over their names, meaning that we do not call people by their names.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. A wicked person's name "rots" because nobody names a child after him, so the name fades away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "rotting" is not physical. It means the name drops out of use. Righteous people's names are given to children and stay alive, but no one wants to use the name of a wicked person, so it disappears.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Decay will come up on their names,
meaning that we do not call others by their names.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רַקְבִּיבוּת תַּעֲלֶה בִּשְׁמוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names of the wicked fall out of use, because no one names children after them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the custom of not naming children after wicked people.

steps.title: רבינא objects from the story of דואג בן יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבי אלעזר with the story of a boy named דואג, the same name as the wicked דואג האדומי. The story tells how his mother gave his weight in gold to the בית המקדש and later, in a famine, ate him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא raised an objection. There was an incident with דואג בן יוסף, whose father left him as a small child with his mother. Every day his mother would measure him in handbreadths and give his weight in gold to the בית המקדש. When the enemy grew strong, she slaughtered him and ate him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts an objection against רבי אלעזר. He brings a story about a boy who was named דואג. The story ends in step 9, and step 10 answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said people do not use the names of the wicked. Yet here a Jewish family named their son דואג, the name of the wicked דואג האדומי from the time of שאול. That seems to show that the names of the wicked were still being used.

keyTerms.meaning: A child in Second Temple times who carried the name of the wicked דואג

steps.confusionAlert: The objection is not about the terrible ending of the story. It is about the boy's name: a family called their son דואג, which seems to go against רבי אלעזר's rule.

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection.
There was an incident with Doeg ben Yosef,
whose father left him as a small child to his mother.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ מוֹדַדְתּוֹ בִּטְפָחִים
phrases.english: Every day his mother would measure him in handbreadths

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתֶנֶת מִשְׁקָלוֹ שֶׁל זָהָב לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: and give his weight in gold to the Temple,
and when the enemy prevailed, she slaughtered him and ate him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's explanation in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that people do not name children after the wicked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A family named their son דואג, the name of the wicked דואג האדומי, so the names of the wicked were apparently still in use.

steps.title: ירמיה's lament and the reply of רוח הקודש finish the story of דואג
steps.stepSummary: The story of the boy דואג ends. ירמיה laments mothers eating their children, and רוח הקודש replies that this was punishment for killing a כהן and נביא in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about her, ירמיה lamented: 'Shall women eat their fruit, the babies measured in handbreadths?' רוח הקודש answers and says: 'Shall a priest and prophet be killed in the Temple of God?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still telling the story that רבינא brought as a challenge. It shows how terrible the boy's end was, and why it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word טפוחים is read as 'measured in handbreadths (טפחים)', hinting at the mother who weighed her son in handbreadths to donate gold. רוח הקודש explains that this horror was punishment for murdering זכריה בן יהוידע, a כהן and נביא, in the מקדש. At this point the challenge still stands: here was a child named after the wicked דואג. Step 10 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: babies in their care; read here as babies measured in handbreadths (טְפָחִים)

phrases.english: And about her Jeremiah lamented:
phrases.notes: About this mother and others like her.

phrases.english: 'Shall women eat their fruit,'
'the babies in their care?'
phrases.notes: Read as 'babies measured in טפחים', like this boy whose weight was measured for the gold gift.

phrases.english: The Divine Spirit answers and says:
'Shall there be killed in the Temple of God'
phrases.notes: The second half of the same verse.

phrases.english: 'a priest and a prophet?'
phrases.notes: Refers to the murder of זכריה בן יהוידע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story in רבינא's challenge from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that people do not name children after the wicked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story shows a real child named דואג, the same name as the wicked דואג האדומי.

steps.title: See what happened to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבינא: look at what happened to this boy. His terrible end proves that a wicked person's name is a bad sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: See what happened to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא's challenge with three words: look how this boy ended up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא wanted to show that people do name children after the wicked. The answer turns his story around: this child had a horrible fate, which shows the name was cursed. So the story actually supports רבי אלעזר: a wicked name brings decay, and that is why people avoid it.

keyTerms.meaning: what became of him, how he ended up

steps.whatToRemember: The story of דואג does not disprove רבי אלעזר. It proves that the name of a רשע is a bad omen.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא admits that this disproves רבי אלעזר. It is saying that when such a name was used, the result was a disaster, which shows the name is a bad omen.

phrases.english: See what became of him.
phrases.notes: The bad name brought a bad end, which supports רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the challenger's evidence into support
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The child named דואג shows that people do name children after the wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The child's terrible fate shows the name was a curse, which confirms why people avoid such names.

steps.title: A righteous person is blessed for himself, a wicked person is cursed with his fellow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a צדיק is praised for his own deeds, while a רשע is cursed even through his wicked companions. He learns this from the singular צדיק and the plural רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A righteous person is blessed from himself, and a wicked person from his fellow. A righteous person from himself, as it is written: 'The memory of the righteous (singular) is for a blessing.' A wicked person from his fellow, as it is written: 'But the name of the wicked (plural) shall rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new teaching based on the same verse in משלי. He points to a difference in the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse, צדיק is singular and רשעים is plural. So a צדיק gets blessing for his own good deeds. But when one רשע is mentioned, his wicked companions are cursed along with him.

keyTerms.meaning: a righteous person is blessed for his own deeds
a wicked person is cursed also through his wicked fellow
the memory of the righteous is for a blessing (משלי 10:7)
the name of the wicked shall rot (משלי 10:7)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A righteous person from himself, and a wicked person from his fellow.
phrases.notes: Blessing comes from his own deeds. The curse spreads to his wicked companions.

phrases.english: A righteous person from himself, as it is written:
'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing,'
and a wicked person from his fellow, as it is written:
'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'
phrases.notes: רשעים is plural, so the wicked are cursed together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: צַדִּיק מֵעַצְמוֹ, וְרָשָׁע מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same verse quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדיק is blessed for his own merit; a רשע is cursed together with his wicked companions.

steps.title: רבינא asks for the source of 'the memory of the righteous is a blessing'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks a scholar who arranged אגדה in front of him where the saying 'זכר צדיק לברכה' comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to one of the Rabbis who would arrange אגדה before him: Where does this saying of the Rabbis, 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing,' come from?
steps.whatsHappening: A new conversation begins. רבינא asks for the source of the familiar phrase 'זכר צדיק לברכה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase was a common saying of the Rabbis. רבינא wants to know which verse it is based on. This question sets up the search for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: arranged or recited teachings of אגדה
where does this matter come from?

phrases.english: Ravina said to one of the Rabbis
who would arrange Aggadah before him:
From where is this matter
that the Rabbis said, 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new search for the source of the phrase used in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the saying 'זכר צדיק לברכה'.

steps.title: The scholar quotes the verse in משלי
steps.stepSummary: The scholar answers that it is written plainly in משלי: 'זכר צדיק לברכה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is written, 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing!'
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar gives the simple answer: the saying is a verse in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is correct but easy, since the saying is an exact quote. The verse is from כתובים, not the Torah itself. That opens the door to the next question.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because it is written:
'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the verse in משלי.

steps.title: Where is it hinted in the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks for a source in the תורה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the תורה, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes further and asks for a hint in the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse in משלי is good, but רבינא wants to find the idea already in the תורה. This sets up the proof from אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: from the Torah, how do we know it?

phrases.english: From the Torah, how do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a deeper source than the answer in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for 'זכר צדיק לברכה'.

steps.title: אברהם is praised as soon as he is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Right after God mentions אברהם's name, the Torah adds praise: 'אברהם will surely become a great and mighty nation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And God said: Shall I hide from אברהם what I am doing?' And it is written: 'And אברהם shall surely become a great and mighty nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar brings the Torah source from the story of אברהם before סדום was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second verse does not seem needed to continue the story. Yet the moment אברהם's name appears, the Torah adds a blessing about him. This shows that mentioning a צדיק brings blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah source for 'זכר צדיק לברכה': once אברהם is mentioned, the Torah immediately blesses him.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And God said:'
'Shall I hide from Abraham'
'what I am doing?'
And it is written: 'And Abraham shall surely become'
phrases.notes: Genesis 18:18, right after his name is mentioned.

phrases.english: 'a great and mighty nation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The praise of אברהם follows directly after his name is mentioned.

steps.title: רבינא asks for the source of 'the name of the wicked shall rot'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא now asks the same question about the opposite saying: 'שם רשעים ירקב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does this saying of the Rabbis, 'The name of the wicked shall rot,' come from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא repeats his question, this time about the curse of the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern of the first half now repeats for the wicked. This sets up a matching answer.

phrases.english: From where is this matter
that the Rabbis said, 'The name of the wicked shall rot'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנַָא הָא מִילְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן ״שֵׁם רְשָׁעִים יִרְקָב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 12, now for the wicked.

steps.title: Again the scholar quotes משלי
steps.stepSummary: The scholar answers that it is written in משלי: 'ושם רשעים ירקב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is written, 'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the scholar first points to the verse in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same easy answer as in step 13. Since it comes from כתובים, רבינא will again ask for a Torah source.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because it is written:
'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּהָא כְּתִיב: ״וְשֵׁם רְשָׁעִים יִרְקָב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the verse in משלי.

steps.title: Again, where is it in the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks for a Torah source for 'שם רשעים ירקב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the תורה, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks again for a source in the חומש, setting up the proof from סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 14 exactly. The answer will mirror the proof from אברהם, but in the negative.

phrases.english: From the Torah, how do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a deeper source than step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for 'שם רשעים ירקב'.

steps.title: סדום is condemned as soon as it is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Right after the Torah says לוט moved toward סדום, it adds that the people of סדום were very wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he pitched his tent as far as סדום.' And it is written: 'And the people of סדום were very wicked and sinful to God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar gives the Torah source for the curse of the wicked, using the story of לוט and סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only had to tell us where לוט lived. But the moment סדום is mentioned, it adds a statement of their wickedness. This mirrors אברהם: mentioning a צדיק brings blessing, and mentioning רשעים brings disgrace.
steps.whatToRemember: אברהם is praised when mentioned, and סדום is condemned when mentioned. These are the Torah sources for 'זכר צדיק לברכה' and 'שם רשעים ירקב'.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And he pitched his tent as far as Sodom,'
and it is written: 'And the people of Sodom'
phrases.notes: Genesis 13:13, right after סדום is mentioned.

phrases.english: 'were very wicked and sinful to God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18, mirroring the proof from אברהם in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The condemnation of סדום follows directly after its name is mentioned.

steps.title: A righteous man among the wicked, a wicked man among the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר describes two opposite people: a צדיק who lived between two רשעים and a רשע who lived between two צדיקים, and neither learned from their neighbors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: There was a righteous man who lived between two wicked people and did not learn from their actions. There was a wicked man who lived between two righteous people and did not learn from their actions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר about the same theme of צדיקים and רשעים. He gives two general descriptions and holds back the names, which the גמרא supplies in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally people are shaped by those around them. רבי אלעזר points to two unusual cases where a person's surroundings had no effect, one for good and one for bad. Because the names come only in the next step, this line works like a riddle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A righteous man lived between two wicked people
and did not learn from their actions;
a wicked man lived between two righteous people
and did not learn from their actions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: צַדִּיק דָּר בֵּין שְׁנֵי רְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on the same צדיקים and רשעים theme that ran through Steps 15 to 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was a צדיק unaffected by wicked neighbors and a רשע unaffected by righteous neighbors.

steps.title: Identifying the two people: עובדיה and עשו
steps.stepSummary: The צדיק among רשעים is עובדיה, and the רשע among צדיקים is עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The righteous man who lived between two wicked people and did not learn from them is עובדיה. The wicked man who lived between two righteous people and did not learn from them is עשו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the names behind רבי אלעזר's two descriptions from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובדיה served in the house of the wicked אחאב and איזבל, yet he stayed God-fearing. עשו grew up in the home of יצחק and רבקה, yet he stayed wicked. This shows that a person's choices can outweigh the influence of his surroundings.

keyTerms.meaning: עובדיה, who served אחאב and איזבל but stayed righteous
עשו, son of יצחק and רבקה, who stayed wicked

phrases.english: A righteous man who lived between two wicked people
and did not learn from their actions: Obadiah.
phrases.notes: The two רשעים are אחאב and איזבל.

phrases.english: A wicked man who lived between two righteous people
and did not learn from their actions: this is Esau.
phrases.notes: The two צדיקים are יצחק and רבקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: צַדִּיק דָּר בֵּין שְׁנֵי רְשָׁעִים וְלֹא לָמַד מִמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם — עוֹבַדְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the names for the two general descriptions in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדיק is עובדיה and the רשע is עשו.

steps.title: Blessing for the righteous implies a curse for the wicked, and the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a blessing given to צדיקים teaches a curse for רשעים, and a curse on רשעים teaches a blessing for צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: From the blessing of the righteous you learn a curse for the wicked, and from the curse of the wicked you learn a blessing for the righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר states a two-sided rule about how the Torah sets צדיקים and רשעים side by side. The next two steps will bring a פסוק for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two are placed next to each other, each one highlights the other. The goodness of the צדיק makes the רשע look worse, and the badness of the רשע makes the צדיק look better. This fits the pattern from Steps 15 to 19, which also used neighboring פסוקים about אברהם and סדום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From the blessing of the righteous
you learn a curse for the wicked;
and from the curse of the wicked
you learn a blessing for the righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבִּרְכָתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים אַתָּה לָמֵד קְלָלָה לָרְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from רבי אלעזר that echoes the juxtaposition theme from Steps 15 to 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessing of צדיקים reveals a curse on רשעים, and a curse on רשעים reveals a blessing for צדיקים.

steps.title: Proof: אברהם's praise is followed by סדום's outcry
steps.stepSummary: The Torah praises אברהם and then right afterward describes the great outcry against סדום and עמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the blessing of the righteous you learn a curse for the wicked, as it is written: 'For I have known him, so that he will command...' And right after it is written: 'And God said: The outcry of סדום and עמורה is great.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove the first half of רבי אלעזר's rule. The praise of אברהם comes directly before the judgment of סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם is praised for teaching his household to do what is right. Right after that comes סדום's outcry. Next to אברהם's goodness, סדום's wickedness looks even worse, so the blessing of the צדיק leads straight into a curse on the רשעים.

keyTerms.meaning: For I have known him (God's praise of אברהם)

phrases.english: From the blessing of the righteous
you learn a curse for the wicked,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי יְדַעְתִּיו לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר יְצַוֶּה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: as it is written: 'For I have known him, so that he will command...'
and it is written right after it:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ זַעֲקַת סְדוֹם וַעֲמוֹרָה כִּי רָבָּה״.
phrases.english: 'And God said: The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: From the blessing of צדיקים you learn a curse for רשעים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:19 to 18:20: praise of אברהם followed directly by the outcry of סדום.

steps.title: Proof: סדום's wickedness is followed by God's blessing to אברם
steps.stepSummary: The Torah calls the people of סדום wicked and then right afterward tells how God spoke to אברם and blessed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the curse of the wicked you learn a blessing for the righteous, as it is written: 'And the men of סדום were wicked and sinful to God.' And then: 'And God said to אברם, after לוט had separated from him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of רבי אלעזר's rule. The shameful description of סדום comes directly before God's blessing to אברם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the order is reversed. The curse on the רשעים comes first, and the blessing of the צדיק follows. Next to סדום's evil, אברם's goodness stands out. This is the same פסוק area used in Step 19 for שם רשעים ירקב.

phrases.english: And from the curse of the wicked
you learn a blessing for the righteous,
as it is written: 'And the men of Sodom were wicked and sinful to God.'
'And God said to Abram,'
'after Lot had separated from him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:14. God goes on to bless אברם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of Step 22, completing the pair begun in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: From the curse of רשעים you learn a blessing for צדיקים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 13:13 to 13:14: סדום's wickedness followed directly by God's blessing to אברם.

steps.title: The world was created even for one righteous person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that the whole world would be created even for a single צדיק, learned from the word טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even for one righteous person the world is created, as it says: 'And God saw the light, that it was good.' And 'good' means only a righteous person, as it says: 'Say of the righteous that he is good.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new teaching about how valuable one צדיק is, and proves it by linking two פסוקים through the word טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At creation, God saw the light כי טוב. Another פסוק calls the צדיק טוב. So the 'good' that God saw in creation hints at the צדיק, which means the world is worth creating even for just one of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the huge worth of a single good person, which is why the Torah takes such care to praise צדיקים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁבִיל צַדִּיק אֶחָד עוֹלָם נִבְרָא,
phrases.english: Even for the sake of one righteous person the world is created,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'And God saw the light, that it was good,'
and 'good' means only a righteous person,
as it says: 'Say of the righteous that he is good.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁבִיל צַדִּיק אֶחָד עוֹלָם נִבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate teaching of רבי אלעזר on the value of צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world is worth creating even for one צדיק, learned from the shared word טוב.

steps.title: Forgetting one's learning causes exile for one's children
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever causes himself to forget part of his learning brings גלות on his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who causes himself to forget something from his learning causes exile for his children, as it says: 'Since you forgot the Torah of your God, I too will forget your children.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר moves to a new topic: the punishment for someone who lets his Torah learning be forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק matches the sin to the punishment. You forgot the Torah, so God will 'forget' your children, which רבי אלעזר explains as exile. The word המשכח means actively causing the forgetting through neglect, not simple human memory loss.

keyTerms.meaning: One who causes himself to forget

steps.confusionAlert: המשכח means someone who causes the forgetting through neglect, such as not reviewing. It does not mean someone who forgets by accident.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who causes himself to forget something from his learning
causes exile for his children,
as it says: 'Since you forgot the Torah of your God,'
'I too will forget your children.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the punishment for forgetting Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Causing oneself to forget Torah brings exile on one's children.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the forgetter is lowered from his position
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the punishment for forgetting one's learning is losing one's high position, learned from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: He is brought down from his greatness, as it says: 'Since you rejected knowledge, I will reject you from serving as a priest for Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different punishment for the same person discussed by רבי אלעזר: he loses his position of importance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו uses the earlier words of the same פסוק in הושע. Rejecting knowledge leads to being rejected from serving as a כהן. רבי אבהו reads this as losing one's high status, while רבי אלעזר focused on the children's exile.

keyTerms.meaning: He is lowered from his greatness (position)
From serving as a כהן for Me

steps.whatToRemember: Forgetting your Torah learning through neglect carries a serious punishment. רבי אלעזר says it brings exile on one's children, and רבי אבהו says it means losing one's position. Both learn it from הושע 4:6.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
He is brought down from his greatness,
as it says: 'Since you rejected knowledge,'
'I will reject you from serving as a priest for Me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: מוֹרִידִין אוֹתוֹ מִגְּדוּלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different punishment for the same case raised in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who causes his learning to be forgotten is lowered from his position.

steps.title: No righteous person dies until another is born
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן teaches that a צדיק never leaves the world until a צדיק like him has been created. He learns this from 'the sun rises and the sun sets,' and illustrates it with עלי and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: No righteous person leaves this world until a righteous person like him has been created. As the verse says, 'The sun rises and the sun sets.' Before the 'sun' of עלי went out, the 'sun' of שמואל from רמה had already started shining.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about צדיקים: the world is never left without a צדיק, because a new one is always in place before the old one passes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the sun rising before it mentions the sun setting. רבי יוחנן reads this order as a lesson: the new 'sun' (צדיק) rises before the old one sets. The example is that שמואל was already a prophet in the משכן before עלי died.

keyTerms.meaning: Departs from the world, meaning dies
'The sun rises and the sun sets' (קהלת א:ה)
שמואל the prophet, from the town of Ramah

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
No righteous person departs from the world
until a righteous person like him is created,
as it is said: 'And the sun rises and the sun sets.'
phrases.notes: The rising is mentioned first, so the new sun comes up before the old one goes down.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּבְתָה שִׁמְשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵלִי,
phrases.english: Before the sun of Eli was extinguished,
the sun of Shmuel of Ramah shone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין צַדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the topic of forgetting one's learning to the earlier theme of צדיקים (step 25), opening a series of רבי יוחנן teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדיק does not die until a replacement צדיק of his level has been born.

steps.title: ה׳ spread the few righteous people across every generation
steps.stepSummary: Also in the name of רבי יוחנן‎: ה׳ saw that צדיקים were few, so He 'planted' them in every generation. The source is 'the pillars of the earth are ה׳'s, and He set the world upon them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: הקדוש ברוך הוא saw that righteous people were few. So He planted them in each and every generation, as the verse says: 'For the pillars of the earth are ה׳'s, and He set the world upon them.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same chain: ה׳ spread out the small number of צדיקים so that every generation would have some.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the צדיקים 'pillars' that hold up the world. If the world rests on them, every generation needs at least one, so ה׳ distributed them instead of placing them all in one era.

phrases.english: (And) Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים מוּעָטִין,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, saw that the righteous were few,
so He arose and planted them in each and every generation,
as it is said: 'For the pillars of the earth are ה׳'s,'
and He set the world upon them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים מוּעָטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same chain (רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן), also about the continuous presence of צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ distributed the few צדיקים across all generations, because the world rests on them.

steps.title: The world exists even for the sake of one righteous person
steps.stepSummary: Also in the name of רבי יוחנן: the world stands even for a single צדיק, as it says, 'The righteous one is the foundation of the world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even for the sake of one righteous person, the world continues to exist. As the verse says: 'And the righteous one is the foundation of the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching in the chain: even one צדיק is enough to keep the whole world standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'צדיק', in the singular, is the foundation of the world, so a single צדיק is enough. This is close to רבי אלעזר's teaching in step 25, but רבי אלעזר spoke about the world being created for one צדיק, while רבי יוחנן speaks about the world continuing to exist for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The righteous one is the foundation of the world' (משלי י:כה)

phrases.english: (And) Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even for the sake of one righteous person
the world exists,
as it is said: 'And the righteous one is the foundation of the world.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁבִיל צַדִּיק אֶחָד הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 29: the world rests on צדיקים, and now even one is enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world continues to exist even for the sake of a single צדיק.

steps.title: רבי חייא brings a different verse as the source
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא, speaking for himself, learns the 'one צדיק' idea from a different פסוק: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא himself said: The source is from here: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא accepts the idea that the world stands for one צדיק, but he offers his own פסוק as the proof. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees on the idea. The only question is which פסוק is the source. רבי חייא reads 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones' as ה׳ preserving the world for the sake of His pious one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones' (שמואל א ב:ט)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya himself said: from here:
'He will guard the feet of His pious ones'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same idea taught in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The world exists even for one צדיק.

steps.title: But 'His pious ones' means many people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא's source: 'חסידיו' is plural, so the פסוק speaks of many pious people, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'His pious ones' implies many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי חייא's proof. His פסוק seems to speak about many צדיקים, so how can it prove that one is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point being proven is about a single צדיק. A פסוק in the plural would show only that ה׳ protects the world for many pious people, which does not support the claim.

phrases.english: 'His pious ones' implies many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's use of 'רגלי חסידיו ישמור' as a source for one צדיק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is plural, so it cannot show that a single צדיק is enough.

steps.title: The word is written in the singular
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is spelled חסידו, 'His pious one', in the singular, even though it is read in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is written 'His pious one' (in the singular).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends רבי חייא's proof by pointing to how the word is actually spelled in the תנ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way the word is read (קרי) is plural, but the way it is written (כתיב) is singular. The singular spelling shows that ה׳ preserves the world even for one pious person, so the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (refers to the spelling, not the reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get confused by the two forms. In the תנ״ך, some words are read one way (קרי) and spelled another way (כתיב). Here the word is read חסידיו (plural) but spelled חסידו (singular), and the proof comes from the spelling.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'His pious one' is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: חֲסִידוֹ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the written spelling (כתיב) differs from the reading (קרי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on how the word is read, the פסוק seemed to speak of many pious people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular spelling means one pious person is enough, so רבי חייא's proof stands.

steps.title: Once most of a person's years have passed without sin, he will not sin
steps.stepSummary: Also in the name of רבי יוחנן: if most of a person's years have passed without sin, he will never sin. The source is the same פסוק, 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Once most of a person's years have passed and he has not sinned, he will not sin anymore, as the verse says: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching in the chain, now using the same פסוק for a new idea: ה׳ protects an established צדיק from sinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Guarding the feet' is read here as ה׳ keeping the pious person from stumbling into sin. Once a person has shown, through most of his life, that he is pious, ה׳ protects him from then on.

phrases.english: (And) Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאוּ רוֹב שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: Once most of a person's years have passed
and he did not sin, he will no longer sin,
as it is said: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאוּ רוֹב שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם וְלֹא חָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 31, now for a new teaching about protection from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After most of his life has passed without sin, a person is protected by ה׳ from sinning.

steps.title: Resisting sin twice brings protection from sin
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי שילא say that if a person has the chance to sin a first and a second time and does not sin, he will no longer sin. They use the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא says: Once a chance to sin comes to a person a first time and a second time and he does not sin, he will not sin anymore, as the verse says: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion on when a person reaches the point where ה׳ guards him from sin. It comes from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן measures this by time (most of a person's life). דבי רבי שילא measure it by tests: resisting an opportunity to sin twice is enough to establish a person as pious, and from then on ה׳ protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house of רבי שילא
A first time and a second time

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'רגלי חסידיו ישמור' is used twice in this section. First it shows that the world exists even for one צדיק, based on the singular spelling חסידו. Then it shows that ה׳ guards a proven צדיק from sin, measured either by most of his years (רבי יוחנן) or by resisting sin twice (דבי רבי שילא).

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
Once a matter of sin comes to his hand
a first time and a second time
and he does not sin, he will no longer sin,
as it is said: 'He will guard the feet of His pious ones.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different measure from step 34 for when a person becomes protected from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Resisting an opportunity to sin twice establishes a person as pious and protected from sin.

steps.title: One who seeks impurity is allowed in; one who seeks purity is helped
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains 'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them, and to the humble He gives grace.' A person who wants to become impure is given an opening, and a person who wants to become pure is helped.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of the verse, 'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them, and to the humble He gives grace'? If someone comes to make himself impure, they open the way for him. If someone comes to purify himself, they help him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains a פסוק about how Heaven responds to a person's choices: bad choices are allowed, and good choices get active help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference in how Heaven treats each choice. For someone choosing sin, Heaven only opens the door and does not stop him. For someone choosing purity, Heaven actively helps him. This fits the previous teachings that ה׳ guards the pious.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
Comes to make himself impure, chooses sin
They open the way for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source that free will is respected in both directions, while Heaven gives extra help to someone who tries to improve.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: What is that which is written:
'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them,'
and to the humble He gives grace'?
If one comes to become impure, they open for him.
If one comes to become pure, they assist him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״אִם לַלֵּצִים הוּא יָלִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of Heaven's role in a person's sin and righteousness, now through a new speaker and a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven allows a person to choose impurity, but actively helps a person who chooses purity.

steps.title: Parable of the seller of naphtha and balsam begins
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל start a parable to explain ריש לקיש's idea: a man who sold both foul-smelling נפט and fragrant balsam.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: This can be compared to a man who was selling naphtha and balsam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a parable that illustrates ריש לקיש's teaching. The parable continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naphtha smells bad and balsam smells pleasant, matching the two choices of impurity and purity. So far this passage only sets up the case. The point of the parable, how the seller treats each customer, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study house of רבי ישמעאל
Naphtha, a crude oil with a bad smell

It is comparable to a man who was selling
naphtha and balsam,
